a1-01.goal: Greet people at different times of day, and ask “How are you?” in both the informal (du) and formal (Sie) way.

grammar.title: du or Sie? Informal and formal
grammar.text:
German has two ways to say “you”.

- **du** (informal): friends, family, children, people your age in casual settings.
- **Sie** (formal): strangers, colleagues you do not know well, officials, your boss. **Sie** is always written with a capital S.

The question “How are you?” changes with it: **Wie geht es Ihnen?** (formal) and **Wie geht es dir? / Wie geht’s dir?** (informal). If in doubt in Germany, start with Sie.
ex: Guten Tag, Frau Kamp. Wie geht es Ihnen?
Hello, Ms Kamp. How are you? (formal)
Hey, Lena! So, how’s it going? (informal)

quiz.q: In the audio course Frau Schneider asks Herr Müller: “Guten Morgen, Herr Müller, wie geht es ___?”
quiz.why: Herr Müller is addressed formally, so the form is Ihnen.

quiz.q: In the video, Emma says “Oh, schön! Die Tasche ist schön!” What is she praising?
quiz.why: die Tasche = the bag.

quiz.q: Which greeting from the audio course is informal, between a grandfather and his granddaughter?
quiz.why: Hey and wie geht’s are casual; Frau Kamp and Ihnen are formal.

quiz.q: It is 8 pm. What do you say when you meet a neighbour?
quiz.why: Morgen = morning, Tag = day, Abend = evening.

quiz.q: What does “Sehr gut, danke.” mean?
quiz.why: sehr = very, gut = good/well.

quiz.q: You meet your new boss, Herr Weber. Which question is correct?
quiz.why: A boss you do not know well is addressed with Sie: Ihnen.

quiz.q: You meet your friend Tom. Complete the question: “Hallo, Tom! Wie geht es ___?”
quiz.why: Friends are addressed with du, and the form after “geht es” is dir.

a1-02.goal: Recognise everyday German words that look like English, and know that every German noun is capitalised and comes with der, die or das.

grammar.title: Nouns: capital letters and der / die / das
grammar.text:
Every German noun is written with a **capital letter** (das Hotel, die Bank). Every noun also has a grammatical gender:

- **der** = masculine
- **die** = feminine
- **das** = neuter

The gender is not always predictable, so always learn a noun together with its article: not “Taxi” but **das Taxi**. The plural of all three is **die**: die Taxis, die Banken.

quiz.q: The man in the taxi says “Ins Zentrum bitte. Zum Königshof.” Where does he want to go?
quiz.why: The driver asks Restaurant or Hotel Königshof, and the man answers: Hotel Königshof.

quiz.q: The taxi driver answers “Okay, kein Problem.” What does he mean?
quiz.why: kein Problem = no problem.

quiz.q: At the end of the episode Nico shouts “Hey, stopp!” What has just happened?
o: He realises his bag has vanished
He has found his aunt Yara
quiz.why: The episode ends with Nico noticing that his bag is gone.

quiz.q: Which noun is correctly written in German?
quiz.why: Nouns always start with a capital letter.

quiz.q: Which article goes with “Flughafen” (airport)?
quiz.why: der Flughafen, masculine.

quiz.q: Complete: “___ Taxi ist da.” (the taxi)
quiz.why: das Taxi is neuter.

quiz.q: “Wo ist das Kino?” What is the person looking for?
quiz.why: das Kino = cinema.

a1-03.goal: Say goodbye politely, formally and informally, and ask for help.

grammar.title: Formal and informal goodbyes
grammar.text:
Just like the greetings, farewells depend on who you talk to.

- **Formal:** Auf Wiedersehen, Herr Tillmanns. (strangers, business, older people)
- **Informal:** Tschüss! / Bis bald! / Mach’s gut! (friends, family)

Asking for help follows the same du/Sie rule: **Brauchst du Hilfe?** (informal) and **Brauchen Sie Hilfe?** (formal).
ex: Auf Wiedersehen, Frau Scholl. Gute Reise!
Goodbye, Ms Scholl. Have a good trip!
Take care, Herbert. See you soon!
All okay? Do you need help?

quiz.q: At the airport a man says “Tschüss, Martina. Gute Reise!” What does “Gute Reise” mean?
quiz.why: die Reise = the trip; gute Reise = have a good trip.

quiz.q: “Auf Wiedersehen, Herr Tillmanns. Gute Reise!” Is this formal or informal?
quiz.why: Auf Wiedersehen plus Herr/Frau is the formal goodbye.

quiz.q: Lisa asks Nico: “Alles okay? Brauchst du ___?” (help)
quiz.why: die Hilfe = help. Nico answers “Ja! Hilfe!”

quiz.q: Nico says “Die Tasche ist weg.” What is gone?
quiz.why: die Tasche = the bag; weg = gone.

quiz.q: Which goodbye would you say to your best friend?
quiz.why: Mach’s gut and Bis bald are informal.

quiz.q: What does “Vielen Dank!” mean?
quiz.why: vielen Dank = thank you very much.

quiz.q: Formal: “Brauchen ___ Hilfe?” (Do you need help?)
quiz.why: Formal you = Sie, and the verb becomes brauchen.

a1-04.goal: Spell your name and address aloud with the German alphabet and ask someone to repeat or spell something.

grammar.title: The German alphabet and special sounds
grammar.text:
The alphabet has 26 letters plus **ä, ö, ü** (umlauts) and **ß** (Eszett, sounds like a sharp “ss”).

Sounds that surprise English speakers:
- **w** = English v (Wasser); **v** = usually f (Vater); **z** = ts (Zeit); **j** = y (ja)
- **ei** = “eye” (nein); **ie** = long “ee” (Bier)
- **sch** = sh (Schule); **s** before a vowel = z (Sonne)
- **st / sp** at the start of a word = sht / shp (Straße, sprechen)

When you spell a word, say each letter name: Emma = E – M – M – A. Practise your own name and your street.
ex: Wie schreibt man das? – E, M, M, A.
How do you spell that? – E, M, M, A.

quiz.q: Nico is looking for someone called Yara. Who is she, according to the video?
quiz.why: Nico says “Meine … aunt?” and Emma helps: “Deine Tante?”

quiz.q: Lisa asks Nico: “Hast du die Adresse? Adresse: Straße, Hausnummer?” What is she asking for?
o: His address: street and house number
quiz.why: die Straße = street, die Hausnummer = house number.

quiz.q: Emma says “Mein Name ist Emma! Und das ist meine Tante.” Who is Lisa to Emma?
quiz.why: Emma explains: “Lisa ist nicht meine Mama. Sie ist meine Tante.”

quiz.q: Complete: “Mein ___ ist Nico.” (name)
quiz.why: der Name = name. Mein Name ist Nico.

quiz.q: You did not understand a word. What do you say?
quiz.why: noch einmal = once more/again.

quiz.q: How is the German letter “w” pronounced?
quiz.why: Wasser sounds like “vasser”.

quiz.q: Which word starts with the sound “sht”?
quiz.why: st at the start of a word is pronounced sht: Straße.
